cultural_notes: the West Side Market (1912) in Ohio City is Cleveland's landmark public market -- a brick-and-tile hall with a clock tower and produce arcade, a civic food anchor (source: en.wikipedia.org West Side Market; westsidemarket.org)

Cleveland has deep Eastern European roots (Slovenian, Polish, Hungarian, Slovak) shaping its food culture, alongside a Puerto Rican community on the near west side (source: general demographic framing, publicly documented)
the Grand River Valley and Lake Erie shore east of the city are Ohio's grape and wine country; Concord grapes are a signature fall crop (source: Ohio wine / grape region framing, publicly documented)

Giant Eagle (a Pittsburgh/Cleveland regional chain), Heinen's (a Cleveland grocer), and Meijer are the metro grocers; Berea sandstone is a characteristic local building stone (source: chain regional footprint; Berea sandstone)
